svg.title: Camera basis derivation diagram with edge case
svg.desc: Shows how forward, right, and up vectors are derived from camera direction, then illustrates the degenerate case when direction equals (0,1,0).

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Why do we normalize the camera direction vector?')
g.text: unit vector pointing where camera looks

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Explain the cross product for the right vector in more detail')
sendPrompt('Why do we cross right × forward rather than forward × right?')
g.text: truly perpendicular up — not world_up itself

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How is half_w used per pixel during ray generation?')
g.text: precomputed scale — no trig per pixel

svg.text: Why not just use world_up directly?
If camera tilts, world_up drifts off-perpendicular.
cross(right, forward) is always exactly orthogonal.
Two parallel vectors have no perpendicular.
The cross product is the zero vector.
Division by length=0. All pixels become NaN → black.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Show me how to detect and fix the degenerate camera direction case in C')

svg.text: dot(a, b) = |a||b|cos θ → parallel vectors give |dot| = 1
Check this at parse time — not per frame.
